fields.meta_description: Build quote automation that reads RFQs, prices lines from your price book, holds low-margin quotes for approval, and follows up before expiry.
fields.h1: Build Quote Automation That Prices Every Request by Your Rules
fields.hero_description: Build quote automation that prices each request from your price book and follows up on every open quote before it expires.
fields.features_heading: The Quoting Rules Emergent Builds Into the App
fields.features_subheading: Each part settles one question a rep would otherwise answer by hand.
fields.feature_1:
Prices that come from one price book

The app prices each line from your price book, unit tiers included, such as 1,000 or more. Keep the book in the app's database, or sync it from your ERP through its API.
fields.feature_2:
Option rules for configured products

Write down which options require or exclude each other, and the app checks every configuration against that list. A quote that breaks a rule stays unsent until it is fixed.
fields.feature_3:
A margin floor with a named approver

The app compares each quote's price with its cost and works out the margin. Set the floor and the approver, and a quote below it waits for that person's yes in Slack or email.
fields.feature_4:
AI that reads emailed RFQs

An AI step reads a request for quote into part numbers and quantities, from an email, a PDF, or a spreadsheet. A rep checks any value the AI is unsure of before it is priced.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders and an expiry date

Pick the days a reminder email goes to the customer and the day the rep takes over. Each quote carries its expiry date, and the dashboard lists open quotes by days left.
fields.feature_6:
Every quote version, in a database you own

Each revision is saved next to the one it replaced, with the person who made it, in a database you own. Paid plans export the app's full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Quotes and the Rule Each One Meets
fields.tab_content_1:
Three RFQ lines, one quantity to confirm

Hollinwade Boatworks emails Quenby Fasteners an RFQ for three parts. The app prices two lines at the 1,000-unit tier: hex bolts x 2,000 come to $840.00 and lock nuts x 1,500 to $270.00, or $1,110.00 so far. The washer quantity was read with low confidence, and the rep, Lisbet Ferraby, confirms it first.
fields.tab_content_2:
15 HP means the 480V panel, or no quote

Anselm Kovacevic builds a quote at Thistlecourt Compressors for Ossory Cabinetworks: a 15 HP compressor at $9,800 with the 230V panel. The option rule says every 15 HP model needs the 480V panel, and until it does, the quote cannot be sent. Anselm switches to the $1,450 480V panel, and the quote totals $11,250.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any margin under 18% goes to Margit

Dorian Pashley at Pendlecote IT prices 12 laptops and setup for Fenwhistle Veterinary Group at $18,000. Against a cost of $15,480, the margin is $2,520. Any quote with a margin under 18% needs the sales manager: the app holds it and sends Margit Brennecke a direct message to approve.
fields.tab_content_4:
Day 10 with no reply goes to Wynona

Gallowmere Signworks sent quote Q-2318 for $4,760 to Pennick Street Bakery. The app emailed the bakery a reminder on day 3 and again on day 7. On day 10 with no reply, it sends the rep, Wynona Desrosiers, a direct message to call, with 20 days left before the quote expires on day 30.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your past quotes and price book into quote automation, then test it on real requests before going live.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write down the rules reps follow
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Hook up your CRM and accounting
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather 20 quotes your team sent last quarter, both won and lost. On each one, mark what the rep typed by hand: the parts, the quantities, the discounts, and the notes. Any field typed the same way twice is one the app can fill.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Clean the price book before you prompt. Give every part one list price, one cost, and the unit tiers that apply, and retire part numbers nobody sells anymore. A quote is only as right as the book it reads from.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the rules reps apply from memory today: which options go together, the lowest margin a quote may carry, and who approves anything below it. Describe the price book and those rules in a prompt, and Emergent builds the quoting app.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect your CRM and accounting system through their APIs, such as HubSpot or QuickBooks. Customer details then come from the CRM and part costs from the accounting records, without anyone retyping them.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose how long a quote stays valid and the days the customer gets a reminder email. Pick the day a quiet quote moves to the rep for a call, and write the reminder in your own words.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Requote 10 past requests through the app and compare each total with the quote your team sent. Include one configuration that breaks a rule and one quote under the margin floor, and check both stop where they should. Fix any rule by prompting.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live on one product line
fields.howto_step_7_des: Start with the product line that gets the most requests, and keep the old process for the rest for a month. Watch the first approvals and reminders closely, adjust the days, then move the next line over.

faq_plan.q: What is the best automated quoting software available?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best automated quoting software available?

prov.original: What is the best automated quoting software available?

faq_plan.a: No single automated quoting software is best for every seller; the best one prices from your own price book and follows your own rules. Check whether it handles your product options, checks margin before a quote goes out, and follows up on its own. Emergent builds a quoting app to those rules from a plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up quote automation?
faq_plan.a: Set it up in three parts: the data (price book and costs), the rules (option limits, margin floor, and approver), and the follow-up (validity and reminder days). In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe all three in one prompt and get a working quoting app. Change any rule later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: How is CPQ quote automation different from a basic quoting tool?
faq_plan.a: CPQ quote automation adds a configuration step that a plain quoting tool skips. CPQ stands for configure, price, quote: software that helps sales reps and self-service customers generate accurate quotes for configurable products and services. It is rules-based and can be customized to address the variables that affect profit margins. Sellers of fixed part numbers may not need it.

faq_plan.q: How do I automate quotes for requests that arrive by email and social media?
faq_plan.a: Send every channel into one request queue, and quote from there. An AI step in the app can read the parts and quantities in an emailed request and send any unclear value to a person. For price questions in comments or direct messages, a social media automation can collect them into the same queue. Ask for quantity and options before you automate quotes for them.

faq_plan.q: What should quote automation put on every quote it sends?
faq_plan.a: Every quote should carry a quote number, the customer, each line with its quantity and unit price, the total, and the expiry date. Add the terms, who prepared it, and how the customer accepts. The quote number matters most once quotes get revised, because it lets the customer and the rep point to the same version.

faq_plan.q: What expiry date should quote automation set on a quote?
faq_plan.a: Set the expiry by how fast your own costs change. If supplier prices hold for a quarter, use 30 days; if they move weekly, use 7 or 14 days and say so on the quote. Print the date on the quote itself, not only in the terms. Have the app recheck prices on any quote a customer accepts after it expires.

faq_plan.q: How should quote automation follow up on quotes nobody has answered?
faq_plan.a: Follow up a set number of times, then hand the quote to a person. Two short reminder emails that each name the quote number and the expiry date are enough before the rep calls. Stop every reminder the moment the customer replies. A quote that expires unanswered can move into a marketing automation workflow that checks back with that customer next quarter.

faq_plan.q: How does quote automation handle a supplier price increase on open quotes?
faq_plan.a: Open quotes either keep their price until they expire or go back for a requote, and you pick which rule the app applies. In an app built with Emergent, every quote sits in a database you own. When the price book changes, the app can list each open quote that contains the affected parts, and the rep decides which to honor.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure whether quote automation is working?
faq_plan.a: Track three numbers from the month before launch onward: the hours from request to quote sent, the share of quotes a rep edits by hand, and the share of quotes accepted. If hand edits stay high after a month, the price book or a rule is wrong. Fix it there before adding more reminders.

faq_plan.q: What should automated quoting software do when a customer accepts a quote?
faq_plan.a: It should lock the accepted version, record who accepted it and when, and pass the order on without anyone retyping it. Mark the deal won in your CRM and send the order to the people who fill it. Those hand-offs belong to your wider sales automation, and apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API to carry the accepted quote across.

plan.angle: The SERP for quote automation is CPQ vendors and listicles that define the term and rank tools. This page shows the four jobs a quoting app does once a request arrives: reading an emailed RFQ into priced line items, enforcing an option rule on configured equipment (the CPQ part), holding a quote under the margin floor for the sales manager, and following up on an open quote before it expires. It stays on the quote itself; the proposal document and signature belong to proposal automation, and the customer-facing request form belongs to the quote form page.
